clue.text: Mark Arctic travels with single cross

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so the word Arctic is rearranged

parts.note: single means one, the Roman numeral I
a cross is the shape of the letter X

explanation.surface: Someone crossing the Arctic alone leaves a mark on a map with a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin, and the medical word for a scar is this Latin term.

clue.text: Rogue is obliged to short Greek slaying dragon

parts.note: a cad is a rogue

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: must means is obliged to

explanation.surface: A villain is compelled to cut short a Greek who kills a dragon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the founder of Thebes killed a dragon and sowed its teeth.

clue.text: Charge overcome by pacifist joining reserve?

definitions.text: Charge overcome by pacifist joining reserve?

indicators.note: in a down entry, being overcome by puts the pacifist on top of the charge

parts.note: a CO is a conscientious objector
a ward is someone in your charge
ice is coldness or reserve of manner

explanation.surface: A conscientious objector signs up for the reserves and faces a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a twist: a pacifist joining the reserves would be the last person to deserve this charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of bravery is the accusation often levelled at conscientious objectors.

clue.text: What's first subtracted from two score to give 10?

indicators.note: the first letter of the opening word is taken away from the word two

parts.note: taken as the word two spelt out

indicators.note: first picks the first letter of What's

parts.note: a score or tally is a running count

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle: what do you subtract from forty to get ten?
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to 10 across, whose definition is utterly; 'two score' looks like forty but is two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely and wholly mean the same as utterly, the definition of the referenced clue.

clue.text: Stress is cut when exercising

indicators.note: letters at exercise are moving about, so is cut is rearranged

explanation.surface: Working out puts a strain on a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry, the rhythmical stress or accent on a syllable.

clue.text: Set of bones found in Saint's birthplace

definitions.meaning: the group of small bones forming the ankle and upper foot
the city in Asia Minor where St Paul was born

explanation.definitionFit: Both an anatomical term for the ankle bones and the ancient city where the apostle Paul was born.

clue.text: Coming to match by car without clubs

indicators.note: the clubs letter is left out of car

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
to match someone is to rival them

explanation.surface: Turning up to a golf match by car without any clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like golf clubs, but is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun for a coming, as in arrival of a train, means the act of getting somewhere.

clue.text: Arab turning up every second in Bild — Sun also

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up reads the letters bottom to top
only every second letter of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: An Arab appears in the German paper Bild and in the Sun too.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of Bild Sun also is IDUAS, which 'turning up' reverses. Bild and the Sun are German and British tabloids.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Saudi Arabia is an Arab.

clue.text: What's no different if served up hot as starter?

definitions.text: What's no different if served up hot as starter?

parts.words: What's no different if served up hot as starter?
parts.note: playful: with the hot letter put first and the whole read upwards, the dish name comes out the same, and it is food served beside a main

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether a dish is any different served hot as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: A side dish is served alongside a main course; the letter trick only plays with the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An accompaniment served with a main course, like chips or salad, is this kind of course.

clue.text: Peaches -—- son's eating mine no longer

indicators.note: the two son letters surround the rest

parts.note: S for son, plus the S of the possessive
ex means former, no longer
a mine is an explosive device, a bomb

explanation.surface: A son eats peaches but no longer from his own supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaches is slang for gorgeous women, and these are slang terms for very attractive women.

clue.text: Utterly depressed child fellow crushed

parts.note: feeling depressed is feeling down
a tot is a small child
he stands for a male person, a fellow
ground means crushed to powder, as coffee beans are

explanation.surface: A boy is utterly miserable, a child flattened by disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom meaning completely or thoroughly, as in suits me perfectly, is a synonym of utterly.

clue.text: North wind in America comes from round the Pole

indicators.note: the north and wind pieces are placed inside the letters for America

parts.note: US is short for United States, America
N is the compass abbreviation for north
to wind something up is to roll it up

explanation.surface: A northerly wind blowing across America originates near the North Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads Pole as the North Pole; the definition is a banner or flag coming off a pole it is wrapped round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled-up banner spreads out when it comes off the staff it is wound round, which is opening flat.

clue.text: Girl competed in one's cups

parts.note: Bev is a girl's name, short for Beverley
to vie is to compete, so competed is vied

explanation.surface: A girl who took part in a contest won some trophies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one's cups' is an old idiom for drunk, not about trophies.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for drunk, matching the idiom of being in one's cups, i.e. intoxicated.

clue.text: I'm crafty, deceptively giving way to husband in town

indicators.note: something deceptive is not as it appears, so the letters of the phrase are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A cunning person cleverly gives in to their husband on a trip to town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' here is the verb meaning to farm or manage land, not a spouse. A city farm lets townspeople keep animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping livestock in an urban setting is farming, i.e. husbandry, done within a city.

clue.text: Authorise bill with tick

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
buying on tick means buying on credit

explanation.surface: Approve a bill with a tick mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tick' looks like a check mark, but is British slang for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To give official approval or recognition is to sanction or empower.

clue.text: British charters, after delay, arriving at African city

indicators.note: the mapmakers' letters follow the delay piece

parts.note: a lag is a delay
OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's official mapmakers, who draw charts

explanation.surface: British charter flights reach an African city late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charters' looks like charter flights, but means makers of charts.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of Nigeria, on the West African coast.

clue.text: Queen given shot before going round the bend

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the bend letter
shot means ruined or broken up, so given is rearranged

parts.note: a U-bend is shaped like the letter U
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A queen is shot before she goes mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' looks like mad, but gives U.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's wife in the legends of the Round Table was a queen.

clue.text: Had conference thrilled: first person to escape from Colditz?

indicators.note: the prisoner piece is placed at the front

parts.note: Colditz was a German WWII prison camp, so an escaper was a POW, prisoner of war
to wow is to thrill

explanation.surface: Prisoners at Colditz held an excited meeting about the first escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is a meeting or discussion, so held a meeting means conferred.

clue.text: Love place to sunbathe, avoiding cold spells

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the cold letter is avoided, so it is dropped from the beach word

parts.note: a beach is a place to sunbathe
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone loves sunbathing on a beach while avoiding cold snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spells' looks like periods of weather, but means magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of Caribbean sorcery, so the word covers witchcraft and magic charms.

clue.text: Very excited when promotion bestowed on Irish politicians

indicators.note: in a down entry the promotion sits on top of the politicians

parts.note: hype is excessive promotion
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Northern Irish politicians get thrilled when they are promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means worked up or overexcited, as in agitated and thrilled.

clue.text: Slap on the face for police force in charge

parts.note: cos is informal for because, and for can mean because
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A police officer gets slapped in the face while in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slap' is theatrical slang for make-up, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap is British slang for make-up, and a product put on to beautify the skin is a beauty preparation.

clue.text: Maybe send to chair meeting businessman with truck

parts.note: an exec is a business executive
a ute is a utility truck, an Australian pickup

explanation.surface: Someone chairs a meeting with a businessman about a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chair' looks like running a meeting, but is the electric chair.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone to death, perhaps by the electric chair, is one way to kill them legally.

clue.text: Spent benefit on food for Christmas when raised

parts.note: use is benefit, as in of use

indicators.note: in a down entry raising the word reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: Christmas pud is the British Christmas pudding

explanation.surface: Benefits are spent on Christmas food when they go up.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted or consumed completely means all gone, as money that has been spent.

clue.text: Tiddly covers band partying

indicators.note: the small word goes round the outside of the band

parts.note: tiddly means very small, as does wee
a hoop is a circular band

explanation.surface: A tipsy crowd covers a band's songs at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiddly' looks like tipsy, but means tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun for boisterous merrymaking, as in making merry, describes lively celebration.

clue.text: Voice dispatching extremists to arrest senior courtier

indicators.note: the remaining letters hold the senior abbreviation inside them
dispatching the outermost letters leaves only the middle

explanation.surface: A spokesman, getting rid of extremists, arrests a senior figure at court.
explanation.definitionFit: The foppish courtier in Hamlet who carries the duel challenge to the prince.

clue.text: They're sat in East End lobbies, tempting woman

indicators.note: the woman is placed inside the lobbies word

parts.note: halls are lobbies, and a Cockney from London's East End drops the H
Eve tempted Adam with the apple

explanation.surface: Women sit in the hallways of East End houses, enticing passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: A-levels are the exams English school students sit at about 18.
explanation.definitionFit: English school-leaving examinations are what students sit, so they are things that are sat.

clue.text: Like chicken pasty

parts.note: as means like
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: Something resembling a chicken pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like a pie, but is the adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey-faced and pale as ash, so pallid and wan, as a pasty complexion is.

clue.text: Promise to embrace Liberal Women's organisation, you and minister, forever

indicators.note: the promise word holds the Liberal letter inside it

parts.note: giving your word is making a promise
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation
thou is an old word for you
to minister to someone is to tend to them

explanation.surface: A pledge to back the Liberals, a women's group, you and a clergyman for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from the doxology used in Christian prayers means for all eternity, everlastingly.

clue.text: Mafia boss following lawyer's repeat instruction

indicators.note: the Mafia boss comes after the lawyer piece

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer
a capo is a Mafia chief

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss takes his lawyer's instructions again.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction telling players to go back to the beginning and play again.

clue.text: Want to stop guard getting heavily involved

indicators.note: the want word stops up the middle of the guard word

parts.note: to keep is to guard
to want is to need

explanation.surface: A guard wants to stop someone getting deeply mixed up in something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sunk up to the joints in something is a figure for being deeply embroiled.
